headline_marked: Health Minister: [[Educated mothers neglecting child care]]
headline: Health Minister: Educated mothers neglecting child care
summary: Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain warns that a lack of proper care and breastfeeding is leaving children vulnerable to diseases.
details: Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain stated that while society has modernized, the level of care provided by parents during child-rearing has declined compared to 40-50 years ago.

Speaking at the opening of World Breastfeeding Week 2026 at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, the Minister noted that mothers from educated and wealthy backgrounds are often neglecting essential child care.

He expressed concern over the alarming rise in C-section deliveries and the fact that many mothers are not providing colostrum—the first milk—which is the most critical and nutritious food for a newborn.

The Minister shared his observations from hospital wards, noting children suffering from measles and malnutrition, with some mothers citing their own poor health and inability to eat properly as a reason.
To combat this, the government plans to implement a one-year action plan, conducting monthly activities in at least one district to raise awareness about the importance of breastfeeding.
The initiative will involve Civil Surgeons, Deputy Commissioners, and Upazila-level officials to establish breastfeeding as an essential practice throughout society.
caption:
Are modern lifestyles compromising our children's health? The Health Minister warns that educated and wealthy mothers are neglecting vital child care.

Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain stated that while society has modernized, the level of care provided by parents during child-rearing has declined compared to 40-50 years ago.

Speaking at the opening of World Breastfeeding Week 2026 at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, the Minister noted that mothers from educated and wealthy backgrounds are often neglecting essential child care.

He expressed concern over the alarming rise in C-section deliveries and the fact that many mothers are not providing colostrum—the first milk—which is the most critical and nutritious food for a newborn.

The Minister shared his observations from hospital wards, noting children suffering from measles and malnutrition, with some mothers citing their own poor health and inability to eat properly as a reason.

To combat this, the government plans to implement a one-year action plan, conducting monthly activities in at least one district to raise awareness about the importance of breastfeeding.

The initiative will involve Civil Surgeons, Deputy Commissioners, and Upazila-level officials to establish breastfeeding as an essential practice throughout society.

Source: Jamuna TV, Somoy News
